statements.impact_statement: Netty epoll native transport vulnerability fixed in 4.2.13.Final. Liquibase is a database migration CLI tool that does not run any network server. netty-transport-native-epoll provides the Linux epoll(7) native transport for outbound client connections. Netty is a transitive dependency from Azure SDK, Cassandra driver, and MongoDB driver — used only as a client-side transport. There is no inbound socket for an attacker to exploit.

statements.status_notes: Netty is a network application framework for development of protocol servers and clients. Prior to versions 4.1.135.Final and 4.2.15.Final, netty_unix_socket_recvFd can leak file descriptors when a peer sends an SCM_RIGHTS control message carrying two descriptors. The issue is reachable via Epoll/KQueue DomainSocketChannel when the application opts into DomainSocketReadMode.FILE_DESCRIPTORS.
statements.impact_statement: Fixed in netty-transport-native-epoll 4.1.135.Final; this repository's current build already resolves that exact version via the Azure extension's Netty HTTP client. NVD states the leak is only reachable through Epoll/KQueue DomainSocketChannel when an application opts into the non-default DomainSocketReadMode.FILE_DESCRIPTORS mode. A source review found no code referencing DomainSocket, DomainSocketChannel, DomainSocketReadMode, EpollDomainSocket, KQueueDomainSocket, recvFd, or SCM_RIGHTS — Liquibase does not use the domain-socket feature the vulnerability requires, regardless of version.
